fix.claim: The Hindu reported that, of the 60,06,675 cases under adjudication when the final roll was published on 28 February 2026, about 11 lakh were in Murshidabad and about 8 lakh in Malda, almost a third of the total, with 4.8 lakh in Uttar Dinajpur.

evidence: There are 60,06,675 cases under adjudication in the final roll published on February 28, 2026. ... including 11 lakh in Murshidabad and eight lakh in Malda. In fact, these two districts bordering Bangladesh have almost one third of cases under adjudication. There are 4.8 lakh cases under adjudication in Uttar Dinajpur
why: The figures are verbatim (1 March 2026) but the text read does not say they came from the CEO's data, so that attribution is removed.

evidence: In terms of absolute numbers, the districts recording the highest number of deletions were Murshidabad (455,137), North 24 Parganas (325,666), Malda (239,375), South 24 Parganas (222,929) and Purba Bardhaman (209,805).
why: Verbatim, with Dakshin Dinajpur at 58.1%, in the article of 8 April 2026, updated 10 April.

evidence: The figures for Murshidabad - 74,775 deletions out of 1,08,400 names that were under adjudication in Shamsherganj, followed by 55,420 out of 99,082 in Lalgola ... More than 37,000 names out of 79,683 under adjudication in Mothabari were struck off the rolls.
why: Verbatim, 'based on collated Election Commission data released on Thursday'; the page did not show its date.

evidence: In the Bahadurpur Kabirajtala village in the Kaliachak block, under the Sujapur assembly seat in Malda, 327 names were deleted from the 444 under adjudication in booth 3. ... the Debipur area of Suti assembly constituency in Murshidabad has voters facing the same issue. In booth 111, a total of 291 names were deleted from the 591 under adjudication.
why: All four booth figures and both places (Sujapur, Malda; Debipur, Suti, Murshidabad) are in the article of 29 March 2026.

evidence: Several voters who were removed from the electoral rolls of West Bengal after the controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise have gheraoed seven judicial officers (JOs) in Malda district's Kaliachak block. ... Malda district has recorded more than 18,000 dead and duplicate voters, while the number of adjudicated electors stands at around 8.30 lakh—a significant figure compared to the total electorate of 29.86 lakh in the district.
why: Verbatim, with the NH 12 blockade, in the report of 1 April 2026.

evidence: seven judicial officers, including three women, were gheraoed by anti-social elements at the BDO office in the Kaliachowk area of Maldah District. ... (vii) Additionally, the Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police, the District Magistrate, Maldah and the Superintendent of Police, Maldah are also directed to show cause ... why: The order PDF (Suo Moto W.P.(C) No. 3/2026, 2 April 2026) says this, including direction (i) on central forces wherever judicial officers adjudicate.

evidence: Visibly taken aback, [CEO, named by office] said, "With directives of the Supreme Court, judicial officers had handled the under-adjudication cases. evidence: Researchers validated 3,85,456 EPIC numbers against the Election Commission of India (ECI) portal, of which 3,72,240 had an appeal recorded. ... Of the 3,72,240 appeals recorded in Murshidabad, 260 were approved and 15 rejected.
why: The figures are verbatim but they are the Civic Research Group's analysis of elector-level EPIC records, a compiler's analysis of named lists that is not an official count.

evidence: Uttar Dinajpur recorded additions from 8.16% of inclusion applications and deletions from 96.11% of deletion requests. The corresponding figures were 8.21% and 98.59% in Jalpaiguri, and 10.58% and 87.71% in Murshidabad. ... Chopra recorded 948 deletions from 954 requests, while only 28 names were added from 28,701 inclusion applications.
